{{Short description|British barrister and statistician (1813-1852)}}
{{Infobox academic|name=Joseph Fletcher|birth_date=1813|death_date=1852 (aged 38–39)|education=[[Middle Temple]] ([[Bachelor of Laws|LLB]])|discipline=[[Law]]<br>[[Statistics]]|workplaces=[[Royal Commission on Hand-Loom Weavers]]|death_place=[[Chirk]], [[Denbighshire]], England}}

{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2019}}
'''Joseph Fletcher''' (1813 – 1852) was an English statistical writer and barrister. He worked also on official committees and as a schools inspector.

==Education==
Fletcher trained as a barrister, entering the [[Middle Temple]] in 1838 and being [[called to the bar]] in 1841. 

== Career ==
Fletcher was the secretary of the [[Royal Commission on Hand-Loom Weavers]].<ref name="ODNB">{{cite ODNB|id=9736|first=Timothy L.|last=Alborn|title=Fletcher, Joseph}}</ref> Starting in 1844, he worked as a [[schools inspector]].<ref name="DNB">{{cite DNB|wstitle=Fletcher, Joseph (1813-1852)|volume=19}}</ref>

From a young age, Fletcher wrote reports on social and health issues.<ref name="DNB" /> These included one on child employment in lead mines, for the Children's Employment Commission 1842.<ref>{{cite web|title=1842 Report - Scottish Mining Website|url=http://www.scottishmining.co.uk/245.html|accessdate=9 February 2017}}</ref> His commission reports influenced legislation. The findings of the children's employment commission in particular laid the basis for parliamentary control. As a schools inspector he wrote also on education.<ref name="DNB" />

In 1850 Fletcher published a ''Summary of the Moral Statistics of England and Wales''; and in the following year a work on ''Education: National, Voluntary, and Free''.<ref name="DNB" /> He was unconvinced of the moral superiority of communities that were relatively sparsely developed, such as small towns and farming areas, presaging views later held by [[Herbert Spencer]] and [[Norbert Elias]].<ref>[http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0952695111399344 Zohreh Bayatrizi, ''Mapping character types onto space: the urban–rural distinction in early statistical writings'', History of the Human Sciences 24(2) 28–47] DOI: 10.1177/0952695111399344</ref> He studied  foreign educational systems, and issued (1851–2) two treatises on ''The Farm School of the Continent, and its Applicability to the Preventive and Reformatory Education of Pauper and Criminal Children in England and Wales''.<ref name="DNB" />

Fletcher was one of the honorary secretaries of the [[Statistical Society of London]]; and also editor of the ''[[Statistical Journal]]''. He was member of the council of the [[British Association]], and acted as secretary to its statistical section.<ref name="DNB" />

== Death ==
Fletcher died at [[Chirk]], [[Denbighshire]] on 11 August 1852. He was buried in the graveyard of [[All Hallows' Church, Tottenham]].<ref name="DNB" />
